artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Gather Up (2021) is a career-spanning compilation by Matt Berry, released on Acid Jazz Records to mark ten years of his collaboration with the label. The album showcases the breadth of Berry’s musical style, blending elements of folk, psych, country, and mellow space rock into a distinctive sound that has become his signature. Highlights include the instantly recognizable “Take My Hand,” the haunting “Badger’s Wake,” and the atmospheric “Solstice,” each reflecting Berry’s knack for merging classic songwriting with a touch of the surreal. The collection draws from his nine studio albums with Acid Jazz, offering both fan favorites and deep cuts that illustrate his evolution as a genre-defying artist.

In his discography, Gather Up serves as both an introduction for new listeners and a celebration for longtime fans, encapsulating the eclectic spirit of Berry’s work over the past decade. The album’s musical style—often described as “folk psych”—is marked by warm melodies, vintage instrumentation, and a subtle sense of irony, all delivered with Berry’s rich, resonant vocals. Critics have praised the compilation for its charm and cohesion, with outlets like Louder Than War highlighting its standout tracks and noting Berry’s status as a true polymath in British music. The release was well-received commercially, reflecting Berry’s growing reputation beyond his work as an actor and comedian.
